evidence.pali: ‘‘Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.
evidence.chinese_simplified: “出息长时，了知：‘我出息长’；入息长时，了知：‘我入息长’。出息短时，了知：‘我出息短’；入息短时，了知：‘我入息短’。学：‘我将觉知全身而出息’；学：‘我将觉知全身而入息’。学：‘我将平静身行而出息’；学：‘我将平静身行而入息’。”
evidence.english: Breathing out long, he knows, 'I am breathing out long'; or breathing in long, he knows, 'I am breathing in long.' Breathing out short, he knows, 'I am breathing out short'; or breathing in short, he knows, 'I am breathing in short.' He trains thus: 'I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body'; he trains thus: 'I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body.' He trains thus: 'I shall breathe out calming the bodily formation'; he trains thus: 'I shall breathe in calming the bodily formation.'

entries.pali: Assā ti imassa ‘‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra’’nti padassa. Codanāsodhanāhī ti anuyogaparihārehi. Eva nti idāni vuccamānākārena.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘此’(assa)是指‘令身行止息’(passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ)这一句。‘通过责问和辨析’(codanāsodhanāhi)是指通过质询与解答(anuyogaparihārehi)。‘如此’(evaṃ)是指现在所说的这种方式。
entries.english: ‘Of this’ refers to this phrase: ‘calming the bodily formation.’ ‘With reproof and correction’ means with questioning and answering. ‘Thus’ means in the manner that is now about to be described.

entries.pali: Katha nti yaṃ idaṃ ‘‘passambhayaṃ…pe… sikkhatī’’ti (paṭi. ma. 1.171) vuttaṃ, taṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena kāyasaṅkhārassa passambhanaṃ, yogino ca sikkhanaṃ hotīti kathetukamyatāya pucchitvā kāyasaṅkhāre sarūpato, oḷārikasukhumato, vūpasamato, anuyogaparihārato ca dassetuṃ ‘‘katame kāyasaṅkhārā’’ tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha kāyikā ti rūpakāye bhavā. Kāyapaṭibaddhā ti kāyasannissitā. Kāye sati honti, asati na honti, tato eva te akāyasamuṭṭhānāpi kāyena saṅkharīyantīti kāyasaṅkhārā. Passambhento ti oḷārikoḷārikaṃ passambhento. Sesapadadvayaṃ tasseva vevacanaṃ. Oḷārikañhi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ avūpasantasabhāvaṃ sannisīdāpento ‘‘passambhento’’ ti vuccati, anuppādanirodhaṃ pāpento ‘‘nirodhento’’ ti, suṭṭhu santasabhāvaṃ nayanto ‘‘vūpasamento’’ ti.
entries.chinese_simplified: （问：）《无碍解道》(Paṭi. ma. 1.171)中所说的‘我将平息……乃至……修学’，那身行的平息，以及瑜伽士的修学，是如何、以何种方式发生的呢？（答：）为了解说此义，通过提问，并从自性、粗细、寂止、问答这几方面来显示身行，故开始了‘什么是身行’等论述。其中，‘身的’(kāyika)是生于色身。‘与身相连的’(kāyapaṭibaddha)是依止于身的。身存在时则有，不存在时则无。因此，它们（入出息）虽然不是由身所生起，但被身所造作，故称为‘身行’。‘平息’(passambhento)是平息粗重的身行。其余二词是它的同义词。确实，使未寂止自性的粗重身行沉静下来，称为‘平息’；使其达到不生之灭，称为‘使其灭’(nirodhento)；善巧地导向寂静自性，称为‘使其寂止’(vūpasamento)。
entries.english: ‘How?’: Having asked out of a desire to explain how, in what manner, the calming of the bodily formation and the training of the yogī occurs—as stated in the passage ‘calming… one trains’—and in order to show the bodily formations in terms of their nature, their grossness and subtlety, their pacification, and in terms of questioning and answering, the passage beginning ‘What are the bodily formations?’ is commenced. Therein, ‘bodily’ means existing in the form-body. ‘Bound to the body’ means dependent on the body. They exist when the body exists and do not exist when it does not. Therefore, even though they do not originate from the body, they are conditioned by the body, and thus are called ‘bodily formations.’ ‘Calming’ means calming the grosser and grosser bodily formation. The remaining two terms are synonyms of that very word. Indeed, one who causes a gross bodily formation, which has an unpacified nature, to settle down is called ‘one who calms’; one who brings it to the cessation that is non-arising is called ‘one who stops’; one who leads it to a thoroughly tranquil state is called ‘one who pacifies.’

entries.pali: Yathārūpehī ti yādisehi. Kāyasaṅkhārehī ti oḷārikehi kāyasaṅkhārehi. Ānamanā ti abhimukhabhāvena kāyassa namanā. Vinamanā ti visuṃ visuṃ passato namanā. Sannamanā ti sabbato, suṭṭhu vā namanā. Paṇamanā ti pacchato namanā. Iñjanā dīni ānamanādīnaṃ vevacanāni, adhimattāni vā abhimukhaṃ calanādīni ānamanādayo, mandāni iñjanādayo. Passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra nti tathārūpaṃ ānamanādīnaṃ kāraṇabhūtaṃ oḷārikaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passambhento. Tasmiṃ hi passambhite ānamanādayopi passambhitā eva honti.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘以如是’(yathārūpehi)即‘以何种’(yādisehi)。‘身行’(kāyasaṅkhārehi)即粗重的身行。‘前屈’(ānamana)是身体向前弯曲。‘旁屈’(vinamana)是向各方分别弯曲。‘遍屈’(sannamana)是全面地或善巧地弯曲。‘后屈’(paṇamana)是向后弯曲。‘动摇’(iñjana)等是‘前屈’(ānamana)等的同义词；或者说，‘前屈’等是强烈的向前移动等，而‘动摇’等是微弱的。‘平息身行’(passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ)是指平息那作为前屈等之因的粗重身行。因为当那（粗重身行）被平息时，前屈等也确实被平息了。
entries.english: ‘Of such a kind’ means ‘of whatever sort.’ ‘With bodily formations’ means with gross bodily formations. ‘Bending forward’ is the bending of the body in a forward-facing manner. ‘Bending aside’ is bending to various sides separately. ‘Bending all around’ is bending everywhere, or bending thoroughly. ‘Bending back’ is bending backward. ‘Shaking’ and so forth are synonyms for ‘bending forward’ and so forth. Or, excessive movements such as moving forward are ‘bending forward’ and so forth, while slight movements are ‘shaking’ and so forth. ‘Calming the bodily formation’ means calming such a gross bodily formation that is the cause of bending forward and so forth. For when that is calmed, bending forward and so forth are also calmed.

entries.pali: Assā ti imassa ‘‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra’’nti padassa. Codanāsodhanāhī ti anuyogaparihārehi. Eva nti idāni vuccamānākārena. Katha nti yaṃ idaṃ ‘‘passambhayaṃ…pe… sikkhatī’’ti vuttaṃ, taṃ kathaṃ kena pakārena kāyasaṅkhārassa passambhanaṃ yogino ca sikkhanaṃ hotīti kathetukāmatāya pucchitvā kāyasaṅkhāre sarūpato oḷārikasukhumato vūpasamato anuyogaparihārato ca dassetuṃ ‘‘katame kāyasaṅkhārā’’ tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha kāyikā ti rūpakāye bhavā. Kāyappaṭibaddhā ti kāyasannissitā. Kāye sati honti, asati na honti, tato eva te akāyasamuṭṭhānāpi kāyena saṅkharīyantīti kāyasaṅkhārā . Passambhento ti oḷārikoḷārikaṃ passambhento.
entries.chinese_simplified: “彼”（Assa）者，是对于“平息身行”（passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ）此句而言。“以质问与澄清”（Codanāsodhanāhi）者，即以诘问与答复（anuyogaparihārehi）。“如是”（Evaṃ）者，即以现在将要讲述的方式。对于所说的“平息……乃至……学习”，因为想要说明“那如何、以何种方式，成为修行者（yogino）对身行的平息与学习呢？”，在提问之后，为了从自性、粗细、止息、问答等方面开示身行，而开始了“什么是身行”等论述。其中，“身的”（kāyikā）意即存在于色身（rūpakāye）中。“与身相联的”（Kāyappaṭibaddhā）意即依止于身（kāyasannissitā）。身存在时它们才存在，身不存在时它们便不存在，正因如此，它们即使并非由身生起，也由身所造作，故为身行。“平息着”（Passambhento）即平息着越来越粗的身行。
entries.english: Of this phrase 'calming the bodily formation.' As for 'codanāsodhanāhi,' it means by means of questioning and answering. As for 'evaṃ,' it means in the manner now being explained. As for 'kathaṃ': having asked, with the desire to explain regarding what was said, 'calming... trains,' 'How, in what manner, does the calming of the bodily formation and the training of the yogi occur?', the passage beginning 'What are the bodily formations?' was commenced in order to show the bodily formations in terms of their nature, in terms of coarseness and subtlety, in terms of pacification, and in terms of questioning and answering. Therein, as for 'kāyikā,' it means existing in the physical body. As for 'kāyappaṭibaddhā,' it means dependent on the body. When the body exists, they exist; when it does not exist, they do not. For that very reason, even those not originating from the body are conditioned by the body; therefore, they are 'bodily formations.' As for 'passambhento,' it means calming the coarsest of the coarse.

entries.pali: Yathārūpehī ti yādisehi. Kāyasaṅkhārehī ti oḷārikehi kāyasaṅkhārehi. Ānamanā ti abhimukhena kāyassa namanā. Vinamanā ti visuṃ visuṃ passato namanā. Sannamanā ti sabbato, suṭṭhu vā namanā. Paṇamanā ti pacchato namanā. Iñjanā dīni ānamanādīnaṃ vevacanāni, adhimattāni vā abhimukhacalanādīni ānamanādayo, mandāni iñjanādayo. Passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra nti tathārūpaṃ ānamanādīnaṃ kāraṇabhūtaṃ oḷārikaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambhento. Tasmiñhi passambhite ānamanādayopi passambhitā eva honti.
entries.chinese_simplified: “如是类”（Yathārūpehi）即“何等类”（yādisehi）。“身行”（Kāyasaṅkhārehi）即粗大的身行（oḷārikehi kāyasaṅkhārehi）。“前屈”（Ānamanā）是身体向前弯曲。“偏屈”（Vinamanā）是向各个侧边弯曲。“遍屈”（Sannamanā）是向各方，或充分地弯曲。“后屈”（Paṇamanā）是向后弯曲。“动摇”（iñjana）等是“前屈”等的同义词；或者，过度的向前移动等是“前屈”等，而轻微的则是“动摇”等。“平息身行”（Passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ）意即平息着那作为前屈等之因的粗大身行。因为当那被平息时，前屈等也就被平息了。
entries.english: As for 'of such a kind,' it means of whatever kind. As for 'by bodily formations,' it means by the coarse bodily formations. As for 'bending forward,' it is the bending of the body towards the front. As for 'bending sideways,' it is bending while looking in various directions. As for 'bending down,' it is bending from all sides, or bending well. As for 'bending back,' it is bending backwards. 'Trembling, etc.' are synonyms of 'bending forward, etc.'; or, 'bending forward, etc.' are excessive movements like moving towards the front, while 'trembling, etc.' are slight movements. 'Calming the bodily formation' means calming the coarse bodily formation of such a kind that is the cause of bending forward, etc. For when that is calmed, bending forward, etc., are also calmed indeed.

entries.pali: Santaṃ sukhuma nti yathārūpehi kāyasaṅkhārehi kāyassa aparipphandanahetūhi ānamanādayo na honti, tathārūpaṃ darathābhāvato santaṃ, anoḷārikatāya sukhumaṃ. Passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra nti sāmaññato ekaṃ katvā vadati. Atha vā pubbe oḷārikoḷārikaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambhento anukkamena kāyassa aparipphandanahetubhūte sukhumasukhumatare uppādetvā tepi paṭippassambhetvā paramasukhumatāya koṭippattaṃ yaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambheti, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘santaṃ sukhumaṃ passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra’’ nti.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘寂静、微妙’（Santaṃ sukhumaṃ）是指：由于有了作为身体不摇动之因的身行，前屈等便不再发生；如此，因无扰动（darathābhāvato）而为‘寂静’，因不粗大（anoḷārikatāya）而为‘微妙’。‘平息身行’是总括而言。或者，行者先平息粗大的身行，然后次第地生起作为身体不摇动之因的、愈来愈微细的身行，再平息它们，乃至平息那达到最极微细顶点的身行，针对此而说‘平息寂静、微妙的身行’。
entries.english: As for 'peaceful and subtle': the bodily formation of such a kind—by which, as they are causes for the body's non-trembling, bending forward and so on do not occur—is 'peaceful' due to the absence of agitation, and 'subtle' due to its non-coarseness. He speaks of 'calming the bodily formation' generally, making it one. Alternatively, having first calmed the coarsest bodily formation, and then having gradually produced subtler and more subtle ones which have become the cause for the body's non-trembling, and having calmed those too, it is with reference to the bodily formation that one calms, which has reached the peak of utmost subtlety, that it was said: 'calming the peaceful, subtle bodily formation'.

entries.work_title: 阿毗达摩入门-名色分别 Abhidhammāvatāro-Nāmarūpaparicchedo
entries.pali: Tato te eva saṅkhāre, passambhentoparūpari; Vutto passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ sikkhatīti ca.
entries.chinese_simplified: 然后他次第地平息这些行；如是所说，他训练自己平息身行。
entries.english: Then, calming those very formations progressively, it is said: 'One trains, calming the bodily formation.'

entries.pali: Vipassanāyaṃ panā ti catudhātuvavatthānamukhena abhiniviṭṭhassa ayaṃ kamo, aññassa cāti veditabbaṃ. Ettakaṃ rūpaṃ, na ito aññanti dassanaṃ sandhāya ‘‘sakalarūpapariggahe’’ ti vuttaṃ. Rūpārūpapariggahe ti ettha aniccatādilakkhaṇārammaṇikabhaṅgānupassanato pabhuti balavatī vipassanā. Pubbe vuttanayenā ti sabbesaṃyeva pana matena apariggahitakāletiādinā. Sodhanā nāma vissajjanaṃ. Assā ti ‘‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāra’’nti padassa.
entries.chinese_simplified: 关于观(vipassanā)，当知，对于以四界分别(catudhātuvavatthāna)为入门而致力于此者，此是其次第；对于致力于其他业处者亦然。所谓‘把握一切色法’，是针对‘色法仅有此量，无有更多’之见而说。于此‘色与非色之把握’中，从以无常等相为所缘的坏灭随观开始，观(vipassanā)变得强大有力。‘如前所说之理’，是依照那些诵师的观点，通过‘于未把握之时’等文句。所谓辨析(sodhanā)，即是解答(vissajjanaṃ)。‘它的’(assa)，是指‘平息身行’(passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ)这一句。
entries.english: Regarding 'But in the case of insight': this is the sequence for one who has entered upon it by way of the determination of the four elements, and for another as well; this should be understood. With reference to the seeing, 'Material form is only this much, there is nothing else besides this,' the words 'in the grasping of all material form' were stated. Here, in 'the grasping of material and immaterial form,' insight is powerful from the contemplation of dissolution onwards, which has the characteristics of impermanence and so on as its object. As for 'By the method stated before': this refers to the method beginning with 'at a time when they were not grasped,' according to the opinion of all. 'Purification' is the name for answering. 'Of it' refers to the phrase, 'calming the bodily formation.'

entries.pali: Vedanādayo ti ādi -saddena saññā gahitā, tenāha ‘‘dve khandhā’’ti. Vipassanābhūmidassanattha nti kāyikasukhādisīsena pakiṇṇakasaṅkhāradassanato vuttaṃ samathe kāyikasukhābhāvato. So ti passambhanapariyāyena vutto nirodho. Vuttanayenā ti imassa hi bhikkhuno pubbe apariggahitakāletiādinā (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.165) kāyasaṅkhāre vuttanayena. Pītisīsena vedanā vuttā ti pītiapadesena vedanā vuttā, sukhaggahaṇato vedanānupassanāpasaṅgatoti adhippāyo. Dvīsu cittasaṅkhārapadesū ti ‘‘cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāra’’nti imesu dvīsu koṭṭhāsesu. Saññāsampayuttā vedanā ti vedanānupassanābhāvato vuttaṃ. Cittapaṭisaṃveditā veditabbā ti ārammaṇato asammohatotiādinā vuttanayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Citta nti jhānasampayuttaṃ vipassanāsampayuttañca cittaṃ. Āmodetī ti sampayuttāya pītiyā jhānavisayāya modeti. Vipassanākkhaṇe tiādinā vuttabhaṅgānupassanakkhaṇe.
entries.chinese_simplified: “受等”，是以“等”字含摄想，因此说“二蕴”。“为示观(vipassanā)地”，是依身乐等为首，以显示杂行而说，因于止(samatha)中无身乐之故。“彼”，是以轻安的方式所说的灭。“依已说之理”，即依于（《波罗夷释义》2.165）中关于“此比丘先前未把握之时”等身行的已说之理。“以喜为首说受”，即是以喜为指称而说受，其意趣为：由执取乐，故与受随观相关。“于二心行句中”，即于“觉知心行，轻安心行”此二部分中。“与想相应的受”，是因其为受随观之故而说。“应知为心所觉知”，是参照“从所缘及无迷惑”等已说之理而说。“心”，即与禅那相应及与观(vipassanā)相应的心。“令喜悦”，即以相应的、以禅那为所缘的喜而喜悦。“于观(vipassanā)刹那”等，是指于已说的坏随观刹那中。
entries.english: 'Feelings, etc.': by the word 'ādi' (etc.), perception is taken; therefore, it says, 'two aggregates.' 'For the purpose of showing the ground for insight': this is said because of showing the miscellaneous formations under the heading of bodily pleasure, etc., due to the absence of bodily pleasure in serenity. 'That': this is cessation, spoken of by the synonym 'calming.' 'By the stated method': by the method stated in the section on the bodily formation with 'for this bhikkhu, at a time when it was not previously comprehended,' etc. 'Feeling is stated under the heading of pīti': feeling is spoken of under the pretext of pīti; the meaning is that because of the grasping of pleasure, it falls under the contemplation of feelings. 'In the two phrases on the mental formation': in these two sections, 'experiencing the mental formation' and 'calming the mental formation.' 'Feeling associated with perception': this is said because it is the contemplation of feelings. 'To be known as experienced by the mind': this is said with reference to the method stated as 'by way of the object, by way of non-delusion,' etc. 'Mind': the mind associated with jhāna and also associated with insight. 'He gladdens': he rejoices with the associated pīti that has the jhāna's object as its domain. 'At the moment of insight': at the moment of contemplating dissolution.
